news.raw_snippet: # Why Nvidia, Not Alphabet, Is the Best Artificial Intelligence (AI) Stock to Own for the Expected $1.75 Trillion SpaceX IPO. Nvidia and Alphabet both stand to profit from SpaceX's upcoming IPO. **Alphabet**'s (GOOGL 0.15%) (GOOG 0.28%) early investment in SpaceX is poised to deliver a generous paper gain, while **Nvidia** (NVDA 1.45%) is quietly positioned to secure sustained growth from the very hardware and artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure that the company must scale following its public listing. Let's explore how both AI giants are connected with SpaceX and assess which one is better positioned for the space race in the long run. According to filings, the SpaceX IPO could approach a valuation of $1.75 trillion or higher, with the potential to raise $75 billion in fresh capital. Investors who invest in Nvidia stock before the SpaceX IPO essentially buy clear, leveraged exposure to the hardware ripple effects that could turn SpaceX's public listing into one of Nvidia's next growth catalysts beyond data centers.

news.raw_snippet: # Ineffable Intelligence: $1.1 Billion Seed Funding At $5.1 Billion Valuation Raised For Reinforcement Learning AI. Follow Pulse 2.0 on LinkedIn. A new artificial intelligence startup founded by a former Google DeepMind leader has raised a record-breaking seed round, according to a CNBC report, underscoring surging investor appetite for next-generation AI systems. Ineffable Intelligence, founded by renowned AI researcher David Silver, secured approximately $1.1 billion in seed funding, one of the largest early-stage financings ever recorded. The round values the company at roughly $5.1 billion and includes participation from major global investors, including Nvidia and Google, as well as leading venture capital firms. The company, launched in late 2025 and headquartered in London, is focused on developing advanced AI systems based on reinforcement learning rather than traditional large language models. The involvement of major technology players, including Nvidia and Google, reflects strategic interest in shaping the next wave of AI infrastructure and capabilities.

news.title: 中国政府禁止Meta收购Manus
news.snippet: 中国监管机构以反垄断为由阻止Meta对AI Agent产品Manus的收购交易，维护市场公平竞争。
news.raw_snippet: # Chinese Government Prohibits Meta's Manus Acquisition. The Chinese government has ordered the prohibition of Meta’s acquisition of the Chinese artificial intelligence (AI) startup “Manus.” The decision came approximately four months after authorities launched an investigation in January into whether the $2 billion (approximately 3 trillion Korean won) deal violated China’s technology export regulations. This marks the first time the Chinese government has directly intervened in capital-raising, acquisition, or merger activities by overseas-based “Chinese” companies. The tech industry assessed that “China has begun cutting off investments from U.S. capital to prevent the outflow of domestic AI talent and technology.”. According to China’s foreign investment law, if a specific foreign capital investment is deemed a threat to national security, the Chinese company receiving the investment is obligated to restore the company to its pre-investment state. In the Chinese tech industry, there are expectations that the so-called “Manus effect”—cutting off U.S. capital and preventing the departure of core technical personnel and executives—will spread.

news.raw_snippet: # Apple’s Next CEO Needs to Launch a Killer AI Product. Tim Cook was a great CEO, but he didn’t crack AI. It’s job number 1 for John Ternus. Sometime in the next year or two, Apple’s new CEO, John Ternus, will step onto a stage and tell the world that his company has a revolutionary product. This product, he’ll say, will put the full and awesome power of AI into everyone’s hands. But if it all works out, that keynote will mark the moment when Apple did to AI what it has done for desktop computers, the internet, mobile technology, wearables and music distribution. That is, it’ll offer a solution to a troublesome technology that’s so delightful and *right* that it seems obvious in retrospect. Current CEO Tim Cook, who announced last week that he’ll vacate his role in September and become the company board’s executive chairman, has done a superlative job guiding the company after Steve Jobs, but he left this important box unchecked.

news.raw_snippet: # Jump, Markel launch AI collaboration. AI artificial intelligence partnership Markel Jump. * Agents and Brokers, Cyber Risks, E&O, Emerging Risks, P/C Insurers, Products & Services, Technology. Artificial intelligence company Jump on Tuesday launched a collaboration with Markel to expand access to Jump’s AI operating system for financial advisers. The collaboration also allows platform users to research and access errors and omissions insurance coverages offered by Markel and then place them through Joseph Caruso & Associates as broker of record, Jump said in a statement. Founded in 2023, Salt Lake City-based Jump provides an AI assistant and intelligence engine built for financial advisers and financial services professionals. There is “a fundamental shift in how risk is managed in the age of AI,” as advisers integrate AI into their businesses, Parker Ence, co-founder and CEO of Jump, said in the statement. “As organizations adopt AI to drive efficiency and better decision-making, risk management must keep pace,” Hollis Zyglocke, regional president, Southeast region at Markel, said in the statement.

news.raw_snippet: HomeBusinessCustomers Bank CEO uses AI clone on earnings call to signal automation push. # Customers Bank CEO uses AI clone on earnings call to signal automation push. ## Customers Bank CEO Sam Sidhu said an AI clone delivered part of the lender's earnings call. The moment underlined the bank's wider push to use OpenAI tools across lending, onboarding and operations. In a move that surprised analysts, the CEO of Customers Bank revealed that the voice delivering part of his company’s earnings call was not his own, but an artificial intelligence clone. Sidhu said the use of an AI clone was intended to signal how seriously the bank is approaching AI adoption. The bank is aiming to use AI not just for productivity gains but as a core part of its operating model. The use of an AI clone on an earnings call may have drawn attention, but the broader story is about how artificial intelligence is beginning to reshape banking operations.

news.snippet: Musk与Altman就OpenAI控制权及AGI发展方向对簿公堂，判决可能影响整个
news.raw_snippet: -- Elon Musk, the Tesla CEO, world's richest man and OpenAI cofounder, took the stand Tuesday in a high-stakes trial revolving around a bitter feud with his former friend Sam Altman that could reshape the future development of artificial intelligence. Musk filed the lawsuit against Altman and his top lieutenant, Greg Brockman, along with Microsoft over its investments in OpenAI, in 2024. In the civil lawsuit, Musk accuses Altman and Brockman of double-crossing him by straying from the San Francisco company's founding mission to be a steward of a revolutionary technology. In his opening statement, Musk's attorney, Steven Molo, quoted OpenAI's mission statement when it was created as a nonprofit for the benefit of humanity, not constrained by the need to generate financial enrichment for anyone. By 2017, about two years after OpenAI's founding, it became clear that OpenAI would need more money, and Molo said the founders eventually settled on the idea of creating a for-profit arm of OpenAI that would support the nonprofit.

news.title: Can Apple’s new CEO turn things around? – Computerworld
news.snippet: What’s not mysterious is that Apple has struggled with AI and it will now be up ...
news.raw_snippet: What’s not mysterious is that Apple has struggled with AI and it will now be up to him to make Apple a real AI player. When Apple rolled out hardware chief John Ternus as the CEO to replace Tim Cook, the reaction was kind but muted. That’s because Ternus has said nothing yet to indicate he has a specific plan to position Apple for the future. I have long been a fan of Apple, but the “i” people have a lot of problems. But the truth is that Apple has spent years without the passion and drive that marked the second coming of Steve Jobs as CEO. The promise of AI was intriguing, but Apple didn’t deliver. As for AI, I would love for the iPhone to actually be intelligent about all of the data swimming within its case. One of the critical talents a CEO at a company as large as Apple needs is either vision or a passion that can pass for vision.
